newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela economy grew 2.8 pct in first half-Rojas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela economy grew 2.8 pct in first half-Rojas.

text.p: Venezuela's economy grew 2.8 percent over the first half of the year, Venezuela's Trade and Industry Minister Freddy Rojas Parra said.
"In the first half of the year, the real oil economy grew by 1.5 percent and the non-oil economy by 3.5 percent. This gives an average of 2.8 percent for the period," Rojas Parra told reporters.
Venezuela's economy contracted by 1.6 percent in 1996 as a whole after a 3.7 percent contraction in the non-oil economy and 4.9 percent growth of the oil economy, he said.
Rojas Parra, who said recently that the economy grew by between one and 1.5 percent in the first half of 1997, did not provide a comparative figure for the first half of 1996.
"We are witnessing a recovery of the gross domestic product which began to show in the second quarter," he said.
Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar added that the growth in the first half of the year indicated that the economy is on target for four percent growth for 1997.
Government officials had indicated earlier in the year that they expected the economy to grow by more than five percent in 1997.
The government's 1998 budget proposal is based on a 5.5 percent target.
